title: This Rainbow Geyser Is Completely Man-Made, By Accident
description:
A surreal, rainbow-colored geyser in the Nevada desert looks like something from another planet. It's man-made, the result of a failed well -- and the famous photos aren't quite as big as they look.

#shorts #sciencefacts #flygeyser #didyouknow
sources: Amusing Planet's "Fly Geyser: A Man Made Geyser in Nevada"
Design You Trust's coverage of Fly Geyser's formation and coloring

scenes.text: This surreal, rainbow-colored geyser in the Nevada desert looks like something out of another planet. It's actually completely man-made, by accident.
In 1964, a company drilled a geothermal test well here, hoping to tap into heat for energy. The water wasn't hot enough for what they wanted, so they tried to seal the well back up.
The seal failed. Pressurized, mineral-rich water started escaping instead, and it's never actually stopped -- continuously building its own mound out of dissolved minerals ever since.
It wasn't even the first accident on this exact spot. A separate well drilled back in 1916, also looking for irrigation water, had already created an earlier mineral cone nearby.

The vivid reds and greens aren't paint or dye. They come from thermophilic algae -- organisms that actually thrive in that hot mineral water, and that can die permanently if a single human hand touches them.
It's also smaller than most photos make it look. Those sweeping shots are usually taken close and low, and the geyser itself only stands a few feet tall.
Did you assume this was a completely natural formation before now?
